review: The supplied manuscript was read in full. The phishing/spear-phishing/whaling distinction and impersonated-versus-targeted person distinction are supported; no substantive rewrite is required.

MITRE T1566 remains Initial Access and lists .001 Attachment, .002 Link, .003 via Service and .004 Voice; current page version 2.8, modified 2026-09-18. DET0070 version 1.0, modified 2026-05-12, supports correlation across mail, file, process, network, and sign-in evidence.
NIST SP 800-63B-4 supports the manual-OTP and verifier-name-binding statements. Add a narrow clarification that FIDO2/WebAuthn is not automatically multi-factor without verified user activation.

The mail-security definitions are broadly sound. Clarify that SPF authenticates an SMTP domain, DMARC requires aligned SPF or DKIM, and a domain policy is a request/input to the receiver's final decision. Current DMARC reference is RFC 9989 (May 2026), which obsoletes RFC 7489 and RFC 9091; reports are specified separately in RFC 9990 and RFC 9991.
The five evidence stages are useful teaching checkpoints, not a mandatory linear attack or incident-response sequence. A payment diversion can happen without credential theft or system compromise.
This review does not establish website publication, browser rendering, or learner completion.
